title: STPT protocol
author: Kannan Umadevi Venkataraju
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.smvec66
materials: Cell type distribution - data processing and structure
This document describes the materials and methods used to process data generated from a Serial 2-photon microscope to quantify the molecular cell types
Each dataset is associated with the following METADATA:
Data processing server (e.g. brain2, brain5 etc.)
The intermediate data are the following:
It has the raw tile file names
Their stage positions in each section
Imaging parameters like laser power etc.
Processing parameters, intermediate processing file names
Log folder has missing tiles info
Cell Type detection & Registration to CCF space

steps.title: Prepare Raw Data
steps.instruction: Organize and clean the raw serial two-photon tomography (STPT) image files.

substeps.instruction: Verify that all sections (.tiff) are saved in both ch1 (red channel) and ch2 (green channel).
Remove ch3 (blank channel) acquisition data using the 'move_test.bat' script.
Transfer ch1 and ch2 raw data to the IBM SONAS server.

steps.title: Configure Reconstruction Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the processing directory and scripts on the processing server (e.g., brain2, brain3, or brain5).

substeps.instruction: Create a process folder named with the project ID.
Copy the reconstruction script into the process folder.
Edit the 'runReconstruction_part1.sh' script using the gedit editor to input relevant data paths.
Update the Mosaic text file located in the ch1 raw data folder.
Update the CH2_TIF_DIR and CH3_TIF_DIR paths.
Update the SECTION_STARTNUMBER and SECTION_ENDNUMBER (e.g., 270) based on the imaging data.
Verify that advanced parameters are set to default.

steps.title: Execute Image Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Run the reconstruction script to generate stitched mosaic files from PMT data.

substeps.instruction: Open the terminal application and change the directory to the processed data directory.
Run the reconstruction script from the terminal command.

steps.title: Perform Reconstruction Quality Control
steps.instruction: Verify the quality of the reconstructed images and the resulting folder structure.

substeps.instruction: Visualize stitched images in Fiji to check overall acquisition quality.
Inspect the 'warping' folder containing 5% downsized image stacks in ImageJ to check for imaging artifacts.
Confirm the presence of 'stitchedImage_ch1' and 'stitchedImage_ch2' folders (1 micron resolution, 50 micron spacing, LZW compressed 16-bit tif).
Confirm the presence of 'averageTile_ch1.tif' and 'averageTile_ch2.tif' used for illumination correction.

steps.title: Perform Image Registration
steps.instruction: Register the downsampled sample brain to the Common Coordinated Framework (CCF) space using elastix.

substeps.instruction: Identify the anterior commissure region in the stitched images.
Use MATLAB to calculate the image intensity mean and standard deviation of the anterior commissure region for both channels.
Determine the warpable range of the stitched brain by comparing start and end coordinates against the 25 micron Allen reference atlas.
Input these values into the prediction script, update channel directories, and run predictions.

Open the registration result file in the 'elastixOutput' folder within 'warping' using the fixed downsized warpable image; synchronize stack slices and mouse pointers to verify congruous edges and corners.

steps.title: Detect Cells and Generate Masks
steps.instruction: Use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) on a CUDA-enabled GPU to detect cells and structures.

substeps.instruction: Select the appropriate network ID based on the signal: '164' for c-fos/nuclear signals, '10' for Mecp2-GFP/intra-nuclear signals, or '313' for subtraction channel based c-fos/nuclear signals.
Locate detected cell masks in the directory: 'statichedImage_ch[n]/[Network ID]'.
Qualitatively assess detection quality by opening cell mask images alongside reconstructed sections with synchronized mouse pointers.

steps.title: Analyze ROI Statistics
steps.instruction: Calculate region-wise cell counts and statistics using MATLAB.

substeps.instruction: Create a Project folder on the processing server containing designated groups for brains and the MATLAB script.
Organize point list text files into appropriate groups (e.g., Group 1 for female brains, Group 2 for male brains).
Run the 'runROI_all' MATLAB script on the processing server to generate a spreadsheet with sample IDs as rows and regions as columns.

steps.title: Compress Raw Data
steps.instruction: Compress the original raw tile folders to save storage space.

substeps.instruction: Run the compression script from MATLAB on the processing server (CPU-intensive, no GPU required).
Document the raw data size before compression (~145 GB) and after compression (~65-75 GB).
